subject: MSA redlines — claim liaison, 72hr notice & evidence preservation
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@synthex.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@synthex.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: MSA redlines + claim liaison & response SLAs

Kimberly / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. Attached is our redline of the MSA and the draft Order Form (Synthex_Redline_MSA_20261203.pdf). A few priority asks from our side so procurement and legal can close quickly: 

- Named claim liaison: we propose Synthex Legal (contracts@synthex.ai) as the initial contact for any third-party IP claim, with a 72-hour initial acknowledgement SLA.
- Evidence preservation: immediate preservation obligation plus an evidence checklist (we included a sample in the attachment).
- Defense control: we prefer a mutual defense approach for third-party claims with the right to assume defense for our downstream customers; however, we are open to a limited carveout for open-source components.
- Insurance: please confirm you can provide proof of insurance (COI) with $5M per-occurrence IP/PL limit or provide alternative language.
- Subrogation / recoveries: we need language preserving the ability to pursue subrogation where applicable.

Can you confirm these points and propose any alternative language you need from your side? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk through the most sensitive bits.

Thanks — attaching the redline.

[Attachment: Synthex_Redline_MSA_20261203.pdf]

Best,
Elena Park
Deputy General Counsel | Synthex.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: MSA redlines + claim liaison & response SLAs

Elena — thanks for the redline and the checklist, and appreciate the clarity on timelines. High level response from Redwood legal: 

1) Acknowledgement vs substantive response: 72-hour initial acknowledgement is reasonable; we usually commit to acknowledge and provide a short triage update within 72 hours. Substantive defense designation/acceptance typically requires additional time (we propose a 30-day window to accept defense or propose counsel).

2) Defense control vs reimbursement: we cannot accept a blanket defend-with-control surrender for all third-party IP claims. Proposed compromise: we accept "defend with control" for claims arising from Customer Content and Customer use, but request a carveback for claims arising from Redwood-managed model outputs where we retain right to elect defense or offer reimbursement — to be handled in the Order Form.

3) OSS carveout: we can accept an open-source component carveout limited to widely used permissive-licensed components (MIT/Apache/BSD). We will need to narrow the definition.

4) Insurance: we can provide a COI. Our typical minimum is $5M general liability and $3M professional liability; we can discuss whether that satisfies your procurement team.

5) Subrogation: we will preserve subrogation rights but ask for mutuality.

6) Evidence preservation checklist: thanks — we reviewed it and attached a short internal checklist with the triage steps we will need from Synthex (evidence_preservation_checklist_v1.docx).

Next steps: Marissa (cc'd) — can you coordinate a short call Tuesday 12/08 10am PT to walk Elena through the defense/control compromise so legal can align with sales and procurement? Elena, if you want a revised blackline before the call we can produce one Monday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
[Attachment: evidence_preservation_checklist_v1.docx]

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from Synthex: 

- The 72-hour timeline we proposed is for initial acknowledgement / triage only; we also proposed that parties begin preservation immediately. Your 30-day window to elect to defend sounds workable as long as there's an interim update at Day 7 if counsel selection is still in flight.
- OSS carveout: our procurement team will accept the MIT/Apache/BSD limitation you suggested but wants the Order Form to list a representative set of flagged components; we can provide that list.
- Insurance: procurement is flexible; COI with $5M / $3M split is acceptable if your policy extends to defense costs for IP claims. Please confirm carrier name and policy number for the COI.
- DocuSign / execution: we will push the redline into DocuSign once language is agreed — I'll send an envelope link.

I've attached an updated redline that reflects the 72-hour acknowledgement + 30-day defense-designation approach (Synthex_Updated_Redline_20261205.pdf). Can you produce Redwood's recommended blackline with the compromise language (defend-with-control limited to Customer Content claims; reimbursement option for model-output claims) before the call?

Best,

Subject: Internal: proposed compromise language for MSA & Order Form (send to Synthex)

Team — draft internal note to send to Synthex summarizing our recommended compromise and redline edits. I'll put this in the blackline we circulate Monday morning. Please confirm by EOD Tuesday so Karthik can update commercial and Marissa can schedule procurement.

Recommended package (high level):
- Notice / liaison: Accept Synthex named liaison + 72-hour acknowledgement. We will commit to an update at Day 7 and final election on or before Day 30.
- Defense / control: "Redwood will accept defense-with-control for third-party claims that allege infringement arising from Customer Content or Customer Configurations. For claims alleging infringement arising solely from Redwood-managed model outputs, Redwood may elect (i) to assume defense with control, or (ii) offer to reimburse reasonable defense costs (reimburse option to include a cap equal to the lesser of the claim value or the Order Form cap)."
- OSS carveout: Narrow to permissive licenses (MIT/Apache/BSD). Add a referenced appendix in the Order Form where both parties can list flagged components.
- Subrogation & mutuality: Preserve mutual subrogation rights; retain right to pursue recoveries.
- Insurance: Offer COI; confirm carrier and policy number prior to signature. Proposed minima: $5M general/third-party liability and $3M professional liability — include defense costs coverage for IP where available.
- Evidence preservation: Use Synthex checklist as baseline; Redwood will provide a short evidence intake form to accelerate triage.

Attachments to send to Synthex: our blackline (to be generated), evidence intake form, and a short FAQ for procurement explaining defend-vs-reimburse tradeoffs.

Related links: DocuSign envelope (pending): https://app.docusign.com/envelopes/123abc456def; HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/9273

Marissa — once Karthik signs off on the commercial implications, can you request procurement to get a COI and confirm carrier info? Karthik — I will include the exact blackline snippet below for cut-and-paste into the MSA.

[Blackline snippet]
"Redwood will defend and control the defense of any third-party claim alleging that the Service, as used in accordance with the Agreement and Customer instructions, infringes a patent, copyright, or trademark. For claims attributable solely to open-source components listed in Appendix A (MIT, Apache, BSD), Redwood's indemnity obligations shall be limited to reasonable remediation assistance. For infringement claims arising from Redwood-managed outputs, Redwood may elect to assume defense or offer reimbursement of documented defense costs as specified in the Order Form."

Please review and flag any commercial risk items. If no major issues, I'll send to Elena and Karthik can attach the updated Order Form pricing worksheet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
